title: Consistent dense mode and scroll-snap behavior for data grids and overlays
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Goal: unify dense-list/table spacing, and normalize scroll snapping and overlay (modal/popover) interactions across browsers for dashboard pages. This ticket covers design decisions, a small prototype, cross-browser quirks inventory, and acceptance criteria for handoff to engineering. Scope: table row density toggles, compact card lists on cost/dashboards, sticky column headers, in-panel charts with scroll-snap behavior, and modal/overlay stacking + scroll locking behavior on mobile and desktop.
acceptance_criteria: Dense mode toggle applies consistent vertical rhythm to tables and cards across Chrome, Firefox, Safari (desktop + iOS Safari); no visual clipping at typical breakpoints (320px -> 1920px)
Virtualized table headers remain visually sticky and aligned with columns when scroll anchoring or GPU transforms are present (no header drift)
Chart panels that use horizontal scroll snap present predictable snap points and accessible keyboard focus order
Overlays (modals, confirmation popovers) lock body scroll on iOS and Desktop without breaking underlying sticky headers or causing layout shift
Design spec includes CSS fallbacks and a developer test matrix with repro steps for at least 6 browser/os combos
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a 'dense' spacing token set that reduces row/card padding and line-height; update layout token map and component variants. 2) For data grids, use overflow: auto on a single scroll container with position: sticky headers and avoid transform() on ancestors; where transforms are necessary, provide a sticky fallback by moving header out of the transformed wrapper via portal. 3) Implement scroll-snap for horizontal chart lists using scroll-snap-type: x mandatory and explicit scroll-snap-align on children; pair with tabindex and aria-roledescription for keyboard users. 4) For overlays, use a robust scroll-lock strategy: apply fixed positioning to body with saved scroll offset for desktop and -webkit-overflow-scrolling: touch + overflow-anchor adjustments for iOS; add focus trap and restore focus on close. 5) Provide feature-detection helpers and CSS fallbacks for Firefox/Safari behaviors and document them in the dev spec.
design_notes: Dense tokens: token.dense.* (spacing, minHeight, icon sizes) — used by TableRow, ListCard, CostRow
Virtualization: ensure row height is consistent between DOM and virtual engine; include header height accounting in measurement hooks

Sticky + transforms: Safari refuses to honor position:sticky if any ancestor uses transform; plan two patterns: portal header or remove transform; recommend avoiding transform for non-animated containers
Scroll snapping pitfalls: fractional pixel rounding can cause off-by-1 px gaps on Safari; use exact pixel widths where possible or a small margin-tolerance in JS snap helpers
Accessibility: snap containers must not trap keyboard users; allow arrow and PageLeft/PageRight navigation and expose current index via aria-live if content is dynamic
tradeoffs: Portal-ing sticky headers simplifies cross-browser consistency but increases DOM complexity and may complicate virtualization boundaries. Heavy reliance on JS for scroll corrections closes gaps in older browsers but increases runtime complexity and test surface. We prioritize predictable production UX; where necessary, accept small JS polyfills for non-critical animations.
open_questions: Should dense mode be global user preference (persisted in profile) or per-route control?
Engineering preference: portal header pattern vs removing transforms from layout containers — which has lower engineering and performance cost in runtime?
How to handle third-party embedded charts that introduce their own scroll containers and transforms?
